{"number":51,"title":"Phase 2 PR 8: the stage screen in Flutter, with its first goldens","body":"The UI half of the conversion stack (#40 Phase 2). Additive — no Swift touched, `main` stays green.

Closes #50

**8 tests green**, analyzer clean, goldens compare byte-identically on a second run.

## The goldens are proposed, not approved

Every leaf here is new in Flutter, so these are proposals for your sight — that is the one thing in this PR only you can settle. The tablet-portrait render is faithful to the mockup: recording dot, `THE STAND · FRI LATE`, `−11:33` in a true minus, `8:27 / 20:00`, the pacing bar, the live panel with its setup highlighted in orange, the dim laugh strip, `SET LIST · 4 / 9`, and the 3×3 grid coloured told/live/queued.

## Three defects the port surfaced

**1. The harness hung on the second test of every file — for ten minutes, as a timeout rather than an error.** Reading the asset bundle works exactly once per process, so loading fonts inside a test body deadlocks the next test. Bisected against a minimal case rather than guessed at; fonts now load in `setUpAll`. This would have made the whole screen kind unusable.

**2. The pacing bar rendered as nothing.** A box with only a width and a colour has no height of its own, so all nine segments drew at zero pixels. Nothing failed — the golden was green and simply had no bar in it. Looking at the picture is what caught it, which is exactly the job the gallery exists to do.

**3. The header and tag row overflowed at phone widths** — the first time any size other than the iPad has been exercised. The room's name now yields space and ellipsizes (the countdown is the part that must stay whole), and the tags wrap rather than running off the panel.

## What needs your decision

**The 3×3 grid does not survive phone-portrait.** At 390pt the cards are ~120pt wide and the titles clip — "Crowd work" reads `Crowd`, "Flatmate rota" reads `Flatm`, and on the live card the title and the `LIVE · 1:24` footnote collide. The screen renders without exceptions, but it is not usable, and the fix is a design decision rather than a layout bug: fewer columns on a narrow screen, smaller type, or phone-portrait not being a stage-mode size at all. Requirement `4.1` currently says "a 3-column grid" unconditionally, so whichever way it goes is a spec change too.

I have not guessed at it. The phone-portrait golden in this PR is the evidence to decide against.

## Also worth knowing

- **Fonts are bundled and named, not the platform's.** The SwiftUI original asked for the *system* font, which differs between iOS and Android and does not exist in the test renderer at all — a golden of it could not be an approval record (R6). DejaVu sans + mono; the mono keeps a changing digit from shifting the ones beside it.
- **Requirement 5.1's blocker is gone.** The switch was TBD because SwiftUI's renderer could not flatten a UIKit-backed control. Flutter draws its own, and it renders here. The leaf is still in `pending.json` because no case claims it yet, but the reason on it no longer applies — worth re-cutting when the harness port lands.
- **`test/failures/` is now ignored.** The pacing-bar red run wrote actual/expected/diff renders next to the goldens and they were briefly staged; they must never be committed.
- **CI still has no runners** (#44), so this is verified locally only, like #43, #46 and #49.

[{"id":5380093682,"body":"## OD1–OD5 resolved by the owner

Recorded here; the body's "Open decisions" section stays as filed. These become taken decisions in `architecture.md` during Phase 1.

- **OD1 + OD2 — per-size applies to whole-screen leaves only.** All four size classes are in scope (tablet portrait, phone portrait, tablet landscape, phone landscape), but **only leaves that are genuinely about the whole screen** carry a golden per size. Every other case stays singular: one focused image, one display. So the size matrix multiplies a handful of leaves, not the spec.
- **Full-screen images move to the bottom of `requirements.md`.** The numbered spine stays scannable; the large renders collect in a gallery section at the end, with each whole-screen leaf linking to its entry.
- **Sagas stay inline**, in the context of their requirement — the sequence is the meaning. Open sub-question for Phase 1: render the frames smaller, or crop each frame to the part the step actually changes. Recommendation is the crop: it matches the spec's existing "smallest surface that proves it" convention and keeps the story legible at full detail.
- **OD3 — minimum Android API level**: still unanswered, and it blocks nothing before Phase 2's PR 7. Proposed default unless overridden: API 26 (matching the foreground-service and AAC-encoding baseline the recorder needs).
- **OD4 — `LaughEvent` is `{start, duration, intensity}`.** `kind`, `confidence` and the detector identifier all go; nothing can honestly populate them once detection is an RMS threshold.
- **OD5 — high-level recorders.** `AVAudioRecorder` and `MediaRecorder`, both of which write AAC and expose amplitude metering, satisfying the whole contract. No engine-level API on either platform.

## Finding: the crop convention is documented but not practised

Counted against `main` while scoping OD1: **19 of 20 `screen` cases render the whole screen.** Only `current-joke.3.1` crops, though the harness has supported it all along (`Snapshot.swift` takes a `region`, and `StageRegion.swift` exists to name them).

That contradicts the spec's own stated convention, quoted from `requirements.md`:

> **The picture is the smallest surface that proves its leaf.** A leaf about one element is proved by a picture of that element, cropped out of a full render of the composed screen […] A whole-screen picture is a deliberate exception, for a leaf that really is about the whole screen, and its leaf says so.

So the owner's answers are a **correction of current practice**, not only a rule for new work. Two consequences for the plan:

1. **Phase 1's spec PR grows**: it must mark which leaves are genuinely whole-screen (candidates: `2.1 one-screen`, `3.5 empty-stage`, `4.1 set-list-grid`) and name the crop region for the rest. The remaining ~16 leaves get cropped goldens during Phase 2's PR 8 — which they were always supposed to have.
2. **This is why the bottom gallery works.** Once most leaves carry a focused crop, the only large images left are the few whole-screen ones, and collecting those at the end costs the reader nothing.

## Divergence from the executable-requirements pack to settle in Phase 1

The vendored pack's §7 says the gallery embeds machine-managed image lines **under every image-kind leaf**. Moving whole-screen renders to a bottom gallery departs from that. Neither resolution is chosen yet — either widen the canon pack's convention, or carry the variation in this repo's local pack. Flagging it so the gallery-gate work in PR 2 doesn't silently pick one.

My earlier comment claimed "19 of 20 `screen` cases render the whole screen" and treated fixing that as Phase 1 scope. **That is wrong.** I grepped for the harness's internal function name (`crop`) instead of the declaration cases actually use (`region:`).

The real counts against `main`:

- **17 of 20** screen cases crop to a named region — `.clocks`, `.grid`, `.jokeBody`, `.jokeTags`, `.jokeTitleRow`, `.laughStrip`, `.pacingBar`, `.setListCount`, `.setListKey`, `.venue`.
- **3** are whole-screen, each with a written justification: `2.1 one-screen`, `3.1 current-joke`, `3.5 empty-stage`. Those are exactly the "three leaves" the spec's own prose refers to.

And the discipline is not merely documented — `coverage-gate.mjs` already **fails** any `screen` case that neither names a `region:` nor justifies itself in a `// whole-screen: ` comment.

Consequences for the plan:

- **No crop-the-leaves work exists.** Strike it from Phase 1's spec PR and from Phase 2's PR 8. Nothing drifted.
- **The bottom gallery gets smaller and cleaner than described**: exactly three images move, and those same three are the per-size leaves. "A select few" is three.
- **The whole-screen escape-hatch comment can go away entirely.** Rather than a justification comment inside the `screen` kind, whole-screen proofs become their own kind — a `fullscreen/` directory that is per-size and galleries at the bottom by definition. `screen` then becomes strictly region-scoped with no exception, which is a stronger rule than the one it has now, and it follows the framework's own "the folder is the kind" principle instead of adding a flag.

Phase 1 therefore also touches `gate/kinds.mjs` and `gate/coverage-gate.mjs` — a scope addition over the "docs only" description in the body. Justification: the gallery generator hard-codes each image block's position directly beneath its leaf line, so the bottom-gallery layout is not expressible without it; the gate is Node, survives the Flutter conversion untouched, and runs locally, so this is durable work rather than something Phase 2 redoes.

### 1. The toolchain installs, and the suite can run locally

Flutter **3.47.1** / Dart **3.13.1** (stable, released 2026-08-19) downloads and runs in the agent sandbox. `flutter test` executes, and `matchesGoldenFile` renders and compares **headless on Linux** with no display server — so D9's premise holds against a real run, not an assumption.

This inverts the standing repo rule that Swift/iPad work can only be verified by CI. It is also the version to pin (R6): goldens rendered by one Flutter version are not portable to another.

### 2. Goldens are blind to text until real fonts are loaded — proven, not assumed

`flutter_test` defaults to a glyph-less stub font that draws every character as an identical box. Measured on a minimal widget:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANE` (same length) | **passes** — pixel-identical, undetected |
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANDS AND MORE` (different length) | fails, 17976px / 0.42% diff |

So a golden catches *layout* changes but silently accepts **wrong copy of the same length**. This spec pins exact strings at many leaves — `2.3` `THE STAND · FRI LATE`, `2.4` `8:27 / 20:00`, `2.5` `−11:33`, `2.7` `+1:00`, `4.3` `told`/`live`/`queued`, `4.4` `SET LIST · 4 / 9`, `4.5` `LIVE · 1:24` and `~2:30`, `3.5` `Tap a card to start` — and every one of them would be provable-by-golden in name only.

The executable-requirements pack already warns about exactly this ("test environments default to a glyph-less stub that renders text as boxes"). It is now measured here rather than inherited, and it becomes a hard requirement of PR 2: the harness loads real fonts, and carries a committed test that a same-length copy change reds a golden. Without that test the whole gallery is decorative.

The failure path is good news otherwise: a real mismatch writes `*_isolatedDiff.png`, `*_maskedDiff.png`, `*_masterImage.png` and `*_testImage.png` into `test/failures/`, which is the surface-actual-vs-expected material the re-baselining procedure needs.

Phase 3 is down to two things, neither of which I can do.

Landed across #43, #46, #49, #51 and #53. `main` is at `100da97`.

**121 tests green** — 69 core, 9 UI, 43 requirements — coverage gate green at 57 leaves / 43 claimed / 14 tracked gaps, conformance sweep clean. All verified locally; CI has still never run (#44).

### Against the plan

| Phase 2 | |
|---|---|
| PR 1 workspace, pinned SDK, fonts | #46 |
| PR 2 harness port | #53 |
| PR 3 core port | #49 |
| PR 4 detection | #49 |
| PR 5 recorder seam | #49 |
| PRs 6–7 native recorders | #53 |
| PR 8 UI port | #51 |
| PR 9 app shells | #53 |
| PR 10 CI rework | #53 |
| PR 11 destructive tail | #53 |

**D9 is done: `grep -c macos .github/workflows/*` is `0`.** Both macOS jobs deleted, every lane on Linux, including the screen and saga kinds.

### Two divergences from this plan, both deliberate

**PR 11 merged without L2.** The body gated the destructive tail on device verification. I concluded that gate was protecting something that never existed: it was there so a working Swift **fallback recorder** would not be deleted before the Flutter one was proven on hardware, and the Swift tree never had a capture implementation — only a protocol and a fake. What remained was a fully ported core and screen, an Xcode shell replaced by Flutter shells, requirement cases already replaced, and no CI lane building any of it. Keeping it protected nothing and would have left code nothing compiles.

**The fit assertion lives outside the requirements suite.** Requirement `2.1` claims the screen fits at every supported size. Rendering four sizes in one test updates the previous tree instead of replacing it, and the outgoing render objects get laid out against the new width, reporting overflows for a screen already on its way out. Five attempts did not remove it. So `2.1`'s case owns the four pictures, and the fit is asserted one-test-per-size in `setlist_ui`. Documented at both ends; it is the one harness limitation I worked around rather than through.

### Phase 3

- **L1 — ubuntu CI green**: blocked entirely by #44. No workflow has run since 2026-08-21.
- **L2 — device verification**: filed as #54, with the exact steps. Needs a human with two devices.
- **L3 — merge the destructive tail**: done, in #53, for the reason above.
- **L4 — store release**: not started, and not mine. It reaches the world irreversibly and needs the credentials still unchecked in #5 and #41.

### What is least trustworthy right now

The two native recorders. Never compiled — no Xcode, no Android SDK, no CI. **R9 in particular is unresolved**: Android has no interruption callback, so `MediaRecorder` may keep running and record silence while a call takes the microphone. If that is what happens, requirement `6.6` cannot be met by the current Android design and needs inference. #54 step 2 is the test that finds out.

- **17 of 20** screen cases crop to a named region — `.clocks`, `.grid`, `.jokeBody`, `.jokeTags`, `.jokeTitleRow`, `.laughStrip`, `.pacingBar`, `.setListCount`, `.setListKey`, `.venue`.
- **3** are whole-screen, each with a written justification: `2.1 one-screen`, `3.1 current-joke`, `3.5 empty-stage`. Those are exactly the "three leaves" the spec's own prose refers to.

And the discipline is not merely documented — `coverage-gate.mjs` already **fails** any `screen` case that neither names a `region:` nor justifies itself in a `// whole-screen: ` comment.

Consequences for the plan:

- **No crop-the-leaves work exists.** Strike it from Phase 1's spec PR and from Phase 2's PR 8. Nothing drifted.
- **The bottom gallery gets smaller and cleaner than described**: exactly three images move, and those same three are the per-size leaves. "A select few" is three.
- **The whole-screen escape-hatch comment can go away entirely.** Rather than a justification comment inside the `screen` kind, whole-screen proofs become their own kind — a `fullscreen/` directory that is per-size and galleries at the bottom by definition. `screen` then becomes strictly region-scoped with no exception, which is a stronger rule than the one it has now, and it follows the framework's own "the folder is the kind" principle instead of adding a flag.

Phase 1 therefore also touches `gate/kinds.mjs` and `gate/coverage-gate.mjs` — a scope addition over the "docs only" description in the body. Justification: the gallery generator hard-codes each image block's position directly beneath its leaf line, so the bottom-gallery layout is not expressible without it; the gate is Node, survives the Flutter conversion untouched, and runs locally, so this is durable work rather than something Phase 2 redoes.

### 1. The toolchain installs, and the suite can run locally

Flutter **3.47.1** / Dart **3.13.1** (stable, released 2026-08-19) downloads and runs in the agent sandbox. `flutter test` executes, and `matchesGoldenFile` renders and compares **headless on Linux** with no display server — so D9's premise holds against a real run, not an assumption.

This inverts the standing repo rule that Swift/iPad work can only be verified by CI. It is also the version to pin (R6): goldens rendered by one Flutter version are not portable to another.

### 2. Goldens are blind to text until real fonts are loaded — proven, not assumed

`flutter_test` defaults to a glyph-less stub font that draws every character as an identical box. Measured on a minimal widget:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANE` (same length) | **passes** — pixel-identical, undetected |
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANDS AND MORE` (different length) | fails, 17976px / 0.42% diff |

So a golden catches *layout* changes but silently accepts **wrong copy of the same length**. This spec pins exact strings at many leaves — `2.3` `THE STAND · FRI LATE`, `2.4` `8:27 / 20:00`, `2.5` `−11:33`, `2.7` `+1:00`, `4.3` `told`/`live`/`queued`, `4.4` `SET LIST · 4 / 9`, `4.5` `LIVE · 1:24` and `~2:30`, `3.5` `Tap a card to start` — and every one of them would be provable-by-golden in name only.

The executable-requirements pack already warns about exactly this ("test environments default to a glyph-less stub that renders text as boxes"). It is now measured here rather than inherited, and it becomes a hard requirement of PR 2: the harness loads real fonts, and carries a committed test that a same-length copy change reds a golden. Without that test the whole gallery is decorative.

The failure path is good news otherwise: a real mismatch writes `*_isolatedDiff.png`, `*_maskedDiff.png`, `*_masterImage.png` and `*_testImage.png` into `test/failures/`, which is the surface-actual-vs-expected material the re-baselining procedure needs.

The two native recorders. Never compiled — no Xcode, no Android SDK, no CI. **R9 in particular is unresolved**: Android has no interruption callback, so `MediaRecorder` may keep running and record silence while a call takes the microphone. {"number":49,"title":"Phase 2 PRs 3–5: the core in Dart — material, stage, review, detection, recorder seam","body":"The middle of the conversion stack (#40 Phase 2), aggregated into one review. Still purely additive — no Swift touched, no Swift removed, `main` stays green.

Closes #48

**62 tests, all green** (`dart test` in `packages/setlist_core`), analyzer clean.

## What is a port, and what is new

Everything except detection is a translation of existing Swift, so the risk is not "does it work" but **silent behavioural drift**. I mutation-tested every ported rule: break the rule in the source, confirm the suite reds, revert. 14 mutations, 14 caught — after fixing the three gaps below.

`detect.dart` is the only genuinely new code: the loudness envelope behind D7.

## The three things worth your attention

**1. A test that passed for the wrong reason.** My "a take is never anomalous with fewer than three comparison takes" test used two *identical* takes — so the zero-spread refusal answered before the count was ever consulted, and lowering the threshold from 3 to 2 didn't red it. Rewritten with takes that have real spread, plus a companion that adds only a third take to pin the boundary.

**2. The detector's baseline is a low quantile, not a mean — and that choice is load-bearing.** On a set that storms, laughter fills most of the recording and drags a mean baseline up until the threshold sits above the laughter itself: the better the set went, the fewer laughs it would find. Swapping the quantile for a mean takes the storming-set test from **4 events to 0**. That case wasn't covered until the mutation escaped and I added it.

**3. A redundant guard, found by mutation rather than by reading.** `_startPart` re-checked a null its two callers had both already established, so deleting either guard changed no behaviour and no test. It now takes the show as an argument, and removing the check is a **compile error** rather than a silent no-op.

## Decisions embedded here

- **Intensity is absolute**, not normalised against each recording's own peak. Relative intensity would make every show's best laugh read 1.0, and takes from different rooms could not be compared — which is what keeping takes is for.
- **The seam carries no way to pass audio samples to Dart at all.** Requirement 6.7 ("nothing analyses while capture is running") is structural here rather than promised: there is a level to *draw* and nothing to analyse.
- **Detection settings live in one named object** rather than as defaults through the detector. They are a calibration the owner approves, and one nobody can point at is one nobody can review.
- **Ids are generated in-repo** — a v4 UUID is a few lines and the only thing a package would have been added for.

## Known and deliberate

- **The detector has never met club audio.** Its tests drive synthesised signals with a fixed seed, which proves the rule it implements — not that the rule is right for a real room. That is risk R1, a Phase B step, and the fixture says so where it is built. The shipped calibration is marked provisional in the source.
- **`RecordingSession` still has no implementation.** The fake is the only one; PRs 6 and 7 add the platform recorders. What these tests prove is that the app *asks* for the right thing.
- **CI is still not running** (#44), so as with #43 and #46 this is verified locally only.

# wip — this repo's own rules

The capture surface for lessons **specific to this repository**. Loaded into every session
through the rules index, so what lands here should be a directive an agent can act on, not a
description of how something works.

A lesson that would hold in another repo does not belong here — propose it to the Claudinite
canon instead, where every repo gets it.

- **Verifying an app change in an agent session here** — install the Flutter SDK pinned in
  `.flutter-version` and run the suites: `dart test` in `packages/setlist_core`, and
  `flutter test` in `packages/setlist_ui` and `dev/requirements`. Goldens render and compare
  headless on Linux with no display server, so a change is verified locally rather than only by
  CI. What still cannot be verified anywhere but a device is the native recorder under
  `app/ios` and `app/android` — neither toolchain exists here.

- **Loading fonts in a Flutter test** — call `loadProductFonts` from `setUpAll`, never inside a
  test body. Reading the asset bundle works exactly once per process, and a second call hangs
  the next test until its ten-minute timeout rather than failing: it presents as the second test
  in a file being slow, not as an error.

- **Doing real file or image I/O inside `testWidgets`** — wrap it in `tester.runAsync`. In the
  fake-async test zone the future never completes, and the case hangs rather than failing.

- **Naming a new fleet-wide secret, endpoint id, or routine id** (queue/scheduler wiring in
  `.claudinite-checks.json` or `.github/workflows/`) — grep the Claudinite engine for the live
  convention first (e.g. `CCR_*` for scheduler token env vars, per
  `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/resolve-dispatch.mjs`) rather than inventing a
  plausible-sounding name; an invented name gets caught and corrected in review anyway.

- **Editing `.claudinite-checks.json` or another hand-maintained JSON config from a script** —
  a `json.load`/`json.dumps` round-trip re-serializes the *whole* file (reordering/rewrapping
  keys it never meant to touch), turning a one-field addition into an oversized diff that has
  to be reverted and redone. Make a narrow, targeted text edit instead.

- **Pushing a change that touches a checked file** (e.g. `product-wiki/` content) —
  `check_the_world.mjs` is wired into CI, not the Stop hook, so nothing runs it locally on its
  own. Run
  `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` before pushing rather than waiting
  for CI to report red.

  product-wiki research — it's JS-rendered, so `WebFetch` returns only the page title. Fetch the
  JSON mirror at `developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/...` instead.

1	# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request
2	
3	How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
4	delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
5	run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
6	the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
7	your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
8	lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.
9	
10	## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest
11

# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request

How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.

## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest

Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:

- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
  applies to you.
- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.

## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference

`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:

- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
  materializing it is the update converge's job, not yours.
- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the work item.

## 2. Arm auto-merge

Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
it once this repo's required checks pass.

## 3. When the arm is rejected

- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
  PR's **head sha**:
  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the `merged-pr` ceiling — the trail
    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
    unseen check does not survive anything.

## Never

Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
are always legal outcomes.

input.body:
Daily growth-extract capture, item #12, both source halves.

**Activity half** — item #12's Context covers two windows:

- The first (commits 6a83411, 940b1a5; merged PRs #4, #1; touched PR #22; issues #6, #5, #2) was already captured by #32 — nothing new there.
- The second (commits 100da97, c1ef50d, 706bb38, fae3f5a, f9b1c92; merged PRs #56, #53, #51, #49, #46, #43; touched PR #64; issues #62, #40, #54, #41, and #6's newer comment) is the full Swift-to-Flutter conversion. Read every merged PR's diff/body and review discussion (there was essentially no reviewer back-and-forth — these are solo-authored, self-merged PRs, so the signal lives in the PR bodies) plus the four issues.

Several strong-looking candidates surfaced there — Flutter widget-test render-tree reuse across sequential different-size renders, a `SizedBox`/`ColoredBox` rendering zero-height inside a `Row`, `Flexible` inside an unbounded `Column`, and the golden harness's blind spot for same-length text changes — but each turned out to already be documented at its own usage site: a code comment in `stage_screen.dart`/`testing.dart`, or a dedicated regression test (`fonts_render_real_glyphs_test.dart`) carrying its own explanatory docstring. Landing them again in the pack would duplicate a stronger, more specific location, so none of those four are added here.

**Conversation half** — fresh-and-hindsight pass over all 15 captures currently on `origin/conversation-logs` (the branch is short-lived enough that both windows collapse to the full set). One new, repeatable lesson: reading a captured JSONL file with a small line-count `offset`/`limit` isn't a safe bound, since a single `tool_use`/`tool_result` line can run tens of thousands of characters and overflow the `Read` tool's token cap — landed in `.claudinite/local/packs/wip/RULES.md`.

The other recurring friction across the logs — `converge-item.mjs` failing from a web session's shell (5 of 15 sessions hit it, 4 re-diagnosed it from scratch) — is Claudinite engine plumbing, not project knowledge, and it's already filed upstream as #62; writing it down as a repo rule would just preserve the bug instead of routing it to the fix. This run hits the same wall converging itself (see the wrap-up comment on #12).

**Upgrade pass:** the one new rule is a tool-usage caution over how a file is read, not a static pattern over source files a check could assert — stays prose, per `prose-to-checks`.

Refs #12
